# Local fields generated by two nearly matching Salem coordinates

<a id="local"></a>
## When a deep translate identifies two local fields

Let \(Y,B\) be algebraic integer units with monic rational minimal polynomials \(f,g\), and let \(p\) be odd.
Choose their images in a common algebraic closure of \(\mathbb Q_p\).
Suppose \(t=v_p(2-YB)>0\) is finite, with \(v_p(p)=1\), and put
\[
 K=\mathbb Q_p(Y),\quad L=\mathbb Q_p(B),\quad E=KL,\qquad
 u=[K:\mathbb Q_p],\quad v=[L:\mathbb Q_p],\quad w=[E:\mathbb Q_p].
\]
Write \(c_f=v_p(|\operatorname{disc} f|)\) and \(c_g=v_p(|\operatorname{disc} g|)\).
Then
\[
       ut(w/v-1)\le c_f,\qquad vt(w/u-1)\le c_g.                    \tag{1}
\]
In particular, if \(K\ne L\), then
\[
                         wt\le 2\max(c_f,c_g).                      \tag{2}
\]
All fields here are the actual subfields for the chosen place.

Every embedding of \(E\) over \(L\) preserves the unique extended valuation and fixes \(2/B\).
Its image of \(Y\) lies at depth at least \(t\) from \(Y\), since \(v_p(Y-2/B)=t\).
There are \(w/v\) distinct images, as \(E=L(Y)\) and the extension is separable.
Thus \(v_p(f'(Y))\ge (w/v-1)t\) by the product of root differences, all other differences being integral.
Among the global conjugates of \(Y\) the \(u\) images obtained by local embeddings of \(K\) have the same derivative valuation.
The norm of that derivative is the discriminant up to sign, and each of its remaining local contributions is nonnegative.
This proves the first inequality in (1).
Exchanging the units gives the second since \(v_p(B-2/Y)=t\).
If \(w=u>v\), then the first left side is at least \(wt\), and the symmetric case follows from the second.
If both \(w/u\) and \(w/v\) exceed one, they are integers at least two.
Multiplying (1) gives \(c_fc_g\ge (wt/2)^2\).
The remaining case \(w=u=v\) gives \(K=L=E\).

<a id="records"></a>
## A dichotomy at the primes carrying positive mass

On the [shrinking adjacent Salem rows](Yin_C_G0901_v210.md#window), put \(D=\deg A\), \(d=\deg B>D\), \(n=[\mathbb Q(A,B):\mathbb Q(A)]\) and \(Y=A^a\) at the specified second exponent below two.
If a fixed finite prime set \(S\) carries normalized translate mass at least \(\delta>0\), the [depth estimate](Yin_C_G0901_v208.md#records) retains mass at least \(\delta/2\) on places of depth \(t\gg_{\delta,S} n/\log n\).
There \(p\ne2\), and at each retained place either \(\mathbb Q_p(A)=\mathbb Q_p(B)\) or
\[
           [\mathbb Q_p(A,B):\mathbb Q_p]\ll_{\delta,S}
                    (d/n)\log(2d)\log(2n).
\]
In particular the latter bound is a fixed power of \(\log(3d)\), up to a constant.
Also if \(n/\log n\) grows faster than \(D\log(2D)\), then \(\mathbb Q_p(A)\subseteq\mathbb Q_p(B)\) at every retained place, including those of small degree.

Indeed \(A^a\) generates the earlier global field by [strict dominance](Yin_C_G0901_v159.md#orbits), so the local fields of \(A^a\) and \(A\) agree.
Its measure is \(A^a<2\) since \(A\) is Salem, and \(M(B)=B<2\) on sufficiently late rows.
For either of the minima of degree \(h\), the Vandermonde determinant bound gives \(\log|\operatorname{disc}|\le h\log h+2(h-1)\log 2\) by bounding each row by \(\sqrt h\max(1,|\alpha|)^{h-1}\).
Equation (2) and the depth bound give the claim, using \(n\gg d/(\log(3d))^{O(1)}\) from the record adjunction estimate.
For the final inclusion \(t>c_f\) eventually, so (1) forces \(w/v=1\).

Thus fixed-prime concentration could persist on coincident local fields of large degree, or on composita of small absolute degree.
The dichotomy controls field coincidence at the prescribed precision and leaves open the value of the translate at such a place.
